themes.title: Anthropic dossier: UAE-linked op, Houthis on Claude
themes.summary: Anthropic published a sweeping global misuse report: an operation it links to the UAE used Claude in influence campaigns aimed at UN experts over Sudan and the Muslim Brotherhood, while Houthi and other armed groups reportedly tried using the model to develop guided weapons and ballistic missiles, with one Houthi missile test apparently failing. The disclosure lands squarely on GCC AI ambitions.
themes.angle: AI governance just became a GCC boardroom and sovereign-risk topic, not a San Francisco debate.

themes.title: UAE rethinks 5GW AI data-campus after Iran strikes
themes.summary: Reuters and others report the UAE is revising its US-backed 5-gigawatt AI data-centre campus plan after Iranian strikes targeted US assets in the Gulf, with reporting ranging from redesign to dismantling the mega-campus. Security now shapes compute geography: the region's flagship AI-infrastructure build is being re-planned around war-risk, not just power and capital.
themes.angle: Compute siting is becoming a national-security decision in the Gulf; data-centre risk models must add missile range.

themes.title: Washington AI panic: Senate safety mandates loom
themes.summary: A week of doomsday warnings has shifted the US debate from whether to regulate AI to how far to go: Senate negotiators are considering requiring AI firms to mitigate known major risks, and members are pressing Speaker Mike Johnson to cancel the House recess over AI safeguards. Axios, Reuters and FT all frame this as regulation finally moving from theory to drafting.
themes.angle: Mandatory risk-mitigation duties would change enterprise AI liability math globally, GCC included.

themes.title: Nvidia eyes up to $10B in Anthropic's mega-IPO
themes.summary: Reuters reports Nvidia is considering investing up to $10 billion in Anthropic's IPO, which could become the largest IPO of all time. The deal would lock Nvidia into Anthropic's compute trajectory, deepening the chipmaker's role as both infrastructure supplier and strategic equity holder in the frontier-model race.
themes.angle: The AI value chain is consolidating: the chip monopolist is underwriting the model maker's public debut.

themes.title: Saudi AI: 14GW compute, Riyadh governance push
themes.summary: Saudi Arabia is partnering with the private sector to build more than 14 gigawatts of AI computing capacity to lure global AI companies, per Economy Middle East, while UNESCO launched ethical-AI governance tools at a global forum in Riyadh. The Kingdom is pairing raw compute with a soft-power regulatory agenda.
themes.angle: Riyadh is positioning itself as both compute capital and the Global South's AI-governance arbiter.

themes.summary: The UAE committed roughly $45-46 billion to Germany in a push centred on AI data centres, and the Germany-UAE Business Forum closed $11.2 billion in deals across 30 agreements. Sovereign Gulf capital is now wiring itself into European AI infrastructure.
themes.angle: Gulf AI capital is going transatlantic; European compute becomes a Gulf strategic-asset class.

themes.title: Inference economics: DeepSeek price pressure, OpenAI demand
themes.summary: DeepSeek's V4.1-Flash release is putting fresh pressure on AI pricing, per The Rundown, while OpenAI is pausing new Pro subscriptions citing demand for GPT-6 Astra, per The Information. The market is squeezing price and capacity at the same time, a squeeze that hits anyone running heavy inference workloads.
themes.angle: Price deflation plus capacity rationing: the two forces defining 2026 inference unit economics.

themes.title: Agentic AI enters production: Perplexity, Cognition on Astra
themes.summary: Perplexity is trusting GPT-6 Astra with end-to-end systems - writing communications, changing software and monitoring production - checking in far less often, per OpenAI, and Cognition uses Astra to help Devin test its own work. OpenAI is seeding the story that long-horizon agents are now dependable enough to run real operations.
themes.angle: The autonomy narrative moved from demos to production load: agents now touch live systems.

themes.title: Oracle's AI capex cash crunch: Ellison sell-down, layoffs
themes.summary: Oracle founder Larry Ellison plans to sell up to $7.5 billion of stock while the company boosts its layoff plan by $700 million, Bloomberg reports, against investor fears the firm is overcommitted to AI data-centre buildout. Even AI infrastructure winners face financing stress as capex outruns cash flow.
themes.angle: The build-now-pay-later AI infra model is hitting its first cash-flow test.

themes.title: China chips rally; fully open K2 models land
themes.summary: Tencent-backed chipmaker Enflame tripled on debut as China pushes chip self-sufficiency, per The Information, while the Institute of Foundation Models released fully open K2 Horizon models with weights, code and training data, per HPCwire. Open-weight supply is broadening exactly as export controls tighten.
themes.angle: Both ends of the stack - silicon and open weights - are de-coupling from US incumbents.
